question.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}k \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -3 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $a⊥b.$ Find the value of $k.$

current_example.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14124529/assets/33b75377650ada38e596de266f364861c62149c1278e979127cc5e7bbcbc4694.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14124529/assets/c8488617fa8b97b1a2a138c845ddc613b6daefbdb0c7e1d431da7f7957e81f0c.svg) are orthogonal vectors, find the value of $k.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since $\mathbf{u}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =5\cdot (-4)+(-3)\cdot 6+k\cdot (-6)+(-2)\cdot 8 \\  & =-20-18-6k-16 \\  & =-6k-54.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the last line to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-6k-54 & =0 \\ -6k & =54 \\ k & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$
